name: Charlie Wilson
role: U.S. representative from Texas (1973–1996); earlier Texas state legislator
summary: Wilson combined support for wage protections, civil rights and abortion rights with military spending and an interventionist foreign policy. He defended arming the Afghan resistance and later called for reconstruction aid. His record also included conservation, support for Somoza, and votes against NAFTA, assault-weapons restrictions and same-sex marriage recognition.

abortion-legal.rationale: His legislative career included sustained support for abortion rights.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: He defended giving weapons to Afghan insurgents and said he would repeat that decision.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: He backed civil-rights legislation and fought discrimination against Black voters.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: He sponsored Texas’s original two-percent sales tax, rather than its abolition.

defeat-communism.rationale: He celebrated defeating Soviet power and defended arming its Afghan opponents.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: His support for the Equal Rights Amendment opposed legal distinctions limiting women’s public role.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: His call to restore military resources to Afghanistan opposed a general withdrawal from foreign commitments.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: His sustained military and financial support for Israel affirmed its continued statehood.

limit-guns.rationale: He voted against the 1994 assault-weapons ban; this does not establish opposition to every firearm safeguard.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: His wilderness protections and effort to stop Rockland Dam preserved natural beauty alongside economic interests.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Hunter’s contemporary account names Wilson among sponsors of legislation codifying the military’s homosexual ban.

racial-franchise.rationale: His campaign against voting discrimination supported Black citizens’ political participation.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: He advocated wage increases and coauthored Texas’s 1969 minimum-wage bill.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He advocated stronger utility regulation in the Texas legislature.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: He argued America owed Afghans reconstruction aid and should have provided a small Marshall Plan.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He voted for DOMA in 1996, denying federal recognition of same-sex marriages.

notes: The full Fresh Air transcript was downloaded; only Wilson’s own responses are treated as direct testimony. The closed UNT 1972 oral history could not be read. The full 1996 appropriations debate and 1978 Observer issue were downloaded and searched. Somoza advocacy is documented without treating a defended ally’s abuses as Wilson’s personal programme; he claimed rights had improved. Arming Islamists does not establish support for religious government. NAFTA opposition alone does not establish a general theory of free trade. Preserve legislation does not establish climate policy or opposition to economic growth. Medicaid support is not universal healthcare. Alleged personal drug use is not drug-legalisation policy; film dialogue is not testimony. No historical inferences were needed.
